difficultyRationale: A frequent early-career mistake: assuming a profile-qualified bean has some implicit fallback when no profile is active.
explanation: A bean annotated `@Profile("prod")` is registered only when `"prod"` is among the active profiles. There is no implicit rule that makes `"prod"` (or any other named profile) active just because nothing was configured; the only profile Spring treats as implicitly active with no configuration is the one literally named `default`, and this bean was never annotated for that. So the bean is never registered, and startup fails wherever `FileStorage` is injected, with an unsatisfied-dependency error.

options.text: Spring creates the bean anyway, because `"prod"` is treated as the implicit default profile whenever no profile is explicitly set — the framework assumes a production environment is the safest fallback when configuration is incomplete.
options.explanation: The implicit profile that applies when none is configured is literally named `default`, not `"prod"`. `@Profile("prod")` only activates under a profile named `prod`.

options.text: The application fails to start wherever `FileStorage` is injected, because the bean is registered only when `"prod"` is active, and no profile — including `default` — makes it active here.
options.explanation: Correct. With no explicit profile and no `@Profile("default")` bean to cover the gap, there is simply no `FileStorage` candidate for Spring to inject.

options.text: Spring activates every profile-qualified bean whose profile name doesn't start with `"!"` whenever no profiles are explicitly configured, treating a bare `@Profile("prod")` the same as an unconditional `@Component` in that situation.
options.explanation: There is no such rule. A bean restricted to a named profile stays inactive unless that specific profile (or, for a negated expression, the absence of it) is actually active.

options.text: The bean is automatically registered under the special `default` profile, since no profiles were configured at all.
options.explanation: A bean only activates under `default` if it is itself annotated `@Profile("default")`. `@Profile("prod")` does not fall back to `default`; it is scoped strictly to the profile named `prod`.
